name: v1.0.1 — the correction that keeps a working route
body: A documentation and archive-integrity release. No behaviour change to the verifiers.
The round-11 dialog archive carried a false impossibility, unmarked.**
The Comfy Cloud in-app agent answered our cloning question with *"DEFINITIVE: No. You cannot wire LoadAudio into the ElevenLabs clone node"* and **recommended dropping voice cloning entirely**.

Cloning works. Job `920dc2e0-e420-473a-9cb9-45b84b0fea65` completed, producing 48 kHz / 3.520 s of speech through exactly that path. The runtime slot is **`files.audio0`** — not the `files.item_1` the node schema advertises — and the platform named it in the first attempt's error. `COMFY_AUTOGROW_V3` is a container declaration, not a wire type.

The reply had never been archived at all; only the outbound brief had. It is now written to the record **with a correction banner**, paired with a verification that refutes it from measurement. Preserved rather than deleted — the archive is the record, and removing a wrong answer destroys the evidence of how it was wrong. Left unmarked, the next session to read it would have dropped a working route.

The gap that allowed it:** the docs contract modelled only `*-brief.md` and `*-verification.md`, so an inbound agent reply was an unclassified file escaping every check. `*-reply.md` is now a first-class kind — it may never name a paste target, and **may never be archived without a paired verification**. An unpaired reply reads as fact.

name: v1.0.0 — verify a generated dub before anyone hears it
body: `pip install fx-dub`**

Your text-to-speech model returned 48 kHz stereo at exactly the right duration and a textbook −18 LUFS. It also said a line you never wrote, in a voice that isn't your character's, with a two-second hole in the middle.
None of that is visible to sample rate and duration. fx-dub gives you two receipts — one for the container, one for **what was actually said** — and exits non-zero when either fails.
| | Catches |
| **`fxdub-receipt`** | a silent dub, a truncated dub, dialogue buried in the bed, a mix that missed its loudness target |

Addressing/typing layer** — `validate_node_input()` transcribed verbatim from ComfyUI's own validator (the client can never be stricter than the server, gated by a zero-rejections corpus test); dotted dynamic-combo fields (`codec.encoding.crf`); presence-aware conditional inputs that raise on inactive-branch values; the output-node guard and the `/history` retrieval contract. New exception: `GraphAddressError`.
3D** — Hunyuan3D-2 image-to-mesh, all core nodes: `client.generate_3d()` → GLB via the existing `/history` + `/view` routes.

Audio** — ACE-Step 1.5 text-to-music (MIT weights, all core, 8 steps/cfg 1) with the duration/seconds coupling invariant enforced from one field; `SaveAudioAdvanced` terminator (the only non-deprecated one); stem separation: `client.generate_audio()`, `separate_audio()`, `upload_audio()`.

name: v3.0.1 — correctness release (first 3.x on PyPI)
body: This is the **first 3.x release to reach PyPI**. v3.0.0 was tagged but its publish run failed at the build stage on a packaging defect, fixed here — see the note on that release.

comfy-headless builds **ComfyUI API-format graphs** and runs them. That means a node name ComfyUI has renamed or removed is a shipped bug: the graph is rejected at submit with an opaque error, and nothing warns you first. This release took that seriously.

A core-only `pip install comfy-headless` could not be imported on Python 3.10–3.13.** `http_client.py` annotated a method `-> httpx.Response` at class level; on a core install `httpx` is absent, so the module sets `httpx = None` and evaluating that annotation at import time raised `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'Response'`.

Two things hid it, and both are now guarded against: the test suite runs where every extra *is* installed, and the maintainer's interpreter is Python 3.14, which defers annotation evaluation under [PEP 649](https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/). A new **static AST test** asserts that any module holding an optional dependency in a possibly-`None` name declares `from __future__ import annotations` — static on purpose, so it cannot be masked by interpreter version or installed extras.

name: v1.2.0 — pinned weights, honest fields, relative verdicts
body: A score is only worth something if you know what produced it, what it read, and when it should have declined. This release is about those three.
Landing page + handbook:** https://mcp-tool-shop-org.github.io/ai-eyes-mcp/
The model revision is pinned to a commit SHA, passed to every load, and **reported in every payload that contains a number**.

Before this, the model resolved to whatever the HuggingFace default branch pointed at *at download time* — so two installs made weeks apart could return different scores for identical input, with no signal and no way for a caller to tell. For a tool whose whole claim is honest measurement, that was the claim failing silently.

`AI_EYES_MODEL_REVISION` is honoured **only** as a different 40-character SHA. `main`, a tag, or an empty string is a hard load failure, not a fallback — falling back would reintroduce exactly the ambiguity the pin removes.
The text encoder holds 64 tokens. A longer query is scored on its prefix. The character cap does not protect you: a 468-character query — under the 500 limit — tokenizes to 119 ids.

name: v2.2.0 — ears and a listening room
body: The release where the instrument got real ears and a listening room.** Every prior release played through synthesized approximations; this one ships a sampled Concert Grand as the default piano and a blind listening room — the Composition Panel — where the composition engine's output is ranked by ear under real listening-test discipline. Around them: a full health pass, receipted public-domain re-sourcing of two library works, and a stranger-test hardening pass over the packed artifact.

`sample` is a first-class server engine and the default when a pack is installed** (`samples/AccurateSalamander` or `AI_JAM_SAMPLES_DIR`); the npm tarball stays sample-free by design. The oscillator piano remains the zero-dependency fallback, now with velocity-shaped brightness (a 1.4–7.2 kHz velocity lowpass) and a gentler master compressor on both synthesis doors.

The cockpit ships its own pruned pack** — 90 OGGs (30 roots at minor-third spacing × 3 velocity layers, ~8 MB) regenerable via a deterministic pruner script with a full provenance manifest (source archive sha256, encoder settings, per-file map). Loads on the first user gesture, plays through the synth's own output chain, falls back seamlessly, and reports its state via `window.__cockpit.samplerState()`. Only the Concert Grand preset routes to samples — the other nine voices keep their synth characters. Samples: Salamander Grand Piano by Alexander Holm, CC-BY 3.0, credited in-app and here.

By ear** — blind pairwise A/B auditions of the composition engine's voicings over real library melodies: reference/A/B clips offline-rendered through the *real* voice path and loudness-matched (attenuate-only, ≤0.5 dB RMS, offsets recorded per trial); seeded, shuffled trial lists with hidden floor catch-trials; Bradley-Terry rankings with bootstrap CIs; a MUSHRA-style >15% post-screen; PROVISIONAL until every pair meets its vote budget and UNINTERPRETABLE when the floor gate fails — first-class outcomes, not errors. Matched-playhead A/B switching with keyboard control; runs persist beside (never inside) the score and export as JSON.

Local models** — the same ranking run by locally installed cross-family LLM judges (one seat per model family; the generator's whole lineage, embedding models, and cloud-routed tags never judge), with per-seat failure marked honestly and never substituted. **History** lists both run kinds; **Compare** reports Kendall τ-b and engine-rank match between a human run and an LLM run, naming a PROVISIONAL or UNINTERPRETABLE human side for what it is.
The panel's engine system honors the maker contract: the local model's voicing spec is repaired by the part-at-a-time refiner before it competes.

name: v1.0.0 — stable interfaces, honest limits
body: A `1.0.0` here is a claim about interfaces, not about pictures.**

The image pipeline still has gaps and the README lists them without softening. Those are not what a major version is about — they get better in *minor* releases. What stops moving is the surface you build against: the CLI, the exit-code contract, the listed import paths, and the two on-disk formats. All of it is enumerated in **[STABILITY.md](https://github.com/mcp-tool-shop-org/prompt-craft/blob/main/STABILITY.md)**, along with what is deliberately *excluded*.

The pre-1.0 ruling was *"a generate that ran is not a stability claim."* Right answer, wrong premise — it argued from **capability**, which is exactly the category that does not block a stable interface. Held only by that argument, the position weakened every time a capability landed.
The real blockers were three markers that read as compatibility checks and were never compared. None appeared on the honest-status table, because none were about the pictures.

`STABILITY.md`** — the covered surface, and at equal length the excluded one: threshold table *values*, `core.optimize`, everything under `subdomains/sprite`, and the identity sub-gate, named **provisional** with `0.55` / `0.05` stated as **unvalidated defaults**. Every name in it is parsed and resolved by a test rather than restated, so the document and the package cannot drift.

`AssetRecord.schema_version`, and a reader that branches on it.** The receipt reader was fail-closed in *both* directions, so any future record change would have invalidated every receipt on disk with no migration path — and `replay` reads receipts written by earlier runs. An absent version reads as v1, so everything already written keeps working. An unknown one raises **`IO_RECORD_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`**, deliberately not `IO_RECORD_INVALID`: "written by a newer prompt-craft" is not "corrupt", and collapsing them would send you off re-binding a perfectly good file.

name: v0.4.0 — the gate reports on itself
body: Nothing in the image path changed in this release.** What changed is that four checks which read as live were doing less than they appeared to — and all four were in this project's own tooling, which is the failure this project exists to catch.
The **lint rule set was inherited** from whatever ruff version resolved, so the gate's meaning moved under a transitive bump and failed a release on unchanged code.
A **`# type: ignore` stopped applying** the moment isort wrapped its import — mypy does not read one on an inner line. A suppression that looked live and was not, found only by a CI-equivalent venv.
`VERIFY OK` named no scope** while the dependency audit sat outside it, inviting the reading that a green `verify.py` is a green CI.
The **lint and typecheck legs covered every file except the one defining them.**

`verify.py --audit`** — the dependency audit as an opt-in leg, off by default because running it makes the gate *time-varying*. Three outcomes rather than two: an advisory **with** a published fix fails; one with **no** published fix is reported without failing; and **could not audit at all** is reported loudest. That third category is not hypothetical — with `[image]` installed, `torch` is a local CUDA build absent from PyPI, so a two-outcome audit would print "no vulnerabilities" while blind to the largest dependency in the tree. Every run names the **extras it resolved against**, because the verdict depends on that set. A pass carrying caveats prints `QUALIFIED`, not a bare OK.

name: v0.3.0 — the encoders landed, and the frame did not carry the plate
body: Every conditioning encoder the contract can express is now wired and covered: SDXL ControlNet OpenPose, IP-Adapter, LoRA, InstantID and regional inpaint; Flux text-only and Fill inpaint.
Two of those paths were run for real instead of mocked, and both are recorded with **what they failed to do**:

Local 5090 `generate()` ran** (seed `169405236028824`, kind `controlnet_ip`, RTX 5090, torch 2.13.0+cu130). The frame came back orcish with crossed arms — no two-hand axe, no triple-bar sigil, no bone-spike bracer. The pose and identity plates did not land.
A live Cloud recipe submit ran** (job `06668d4c`). In-graph crop, no diptych; the Fill kept the bracer.
Wired and fake-tested is not the plate landing in the pixels. The status table says so.

Also in this release: two IP-Adapter plates stay on one adapter (both images kept; `requested_scale` and the applied `scale` are both recorded on the receipt); `bind --no-mock` is a real door rather than a claim about a missing extra; Tier-2 is a real DSG expansion; a live GEPA compile ran on local Ollama `hermes3:8b` and pinned `sprite.synth.v1-gepa.json` — that is not a 600B compile, and the per-asset loop still uses `TemplateSynthesizer`.

name: v0.2.1 — the packaging the first release should have carried
body: No behaviour changed.** Same 105 tests, same gate, same exit contract. This release fixes two registry pages that were wrong within minutes of v0.2.0.

`npm/` carried a LICENSE and no README beside it. npm serves the **latest version's** README, so even the placeholder's one-line description disappeared the moment 0.2.0 landed with none. The package now carries its own README — with the logo as an **absolute** URL, because npm renders only absolute image URLs and a repo-relative `` shows nothing.

The GitHub front door opens with a logo at `docs/assets/logo.png` and a seven-language nav bar of sibling files. On PyPI, which has no repository around it, all nine of those were dead links. `README.pypi.md` carries the same content with nothing relative in it.
`project.urls` also carried only the repository — Homepage, Documentation, Changelog and Issues now resolve from the PyPI sidebar.

Recorded plainly: the studio's own publish checklist names both of these failures, and the step that would have caught them — `npm pack --dry-run` **before** the release commit — was run afterwards instead. Shipcheck read 100% throughout, because a missing README inside a subdirectory package is not one of its gates. The gate was green and the artifact was wrong.

Verified before this tag rather than after: `twine check` PASSED on wheel and sdist, `npm pack` lists `README.md`, the logo URL is absolute, and all eight README files carry v0.2.1 and the full exit-code table.

name: v0.3.0 — the spend gate
body: A spend that cannot name its subject creates nothing.**

Cloud generation costs real credits and spent credits have no compensator. Until now the bound on that was a line in each experiment's spec, honoured by whoever read it — a document discipline, and this repo's method exists because those fail quietly.

A subject's canon is a machine-readable statement of what the character **is**, keyed on surface. A surface with no occupant is recorded as a **hole rather than an absence**, because an element list cannot show what it omitted.

The router checks **both directions** — that the submission covers the canon, and that everything in the submission *is* canon. The reverse direction is the one that discriminates: a prompt naming a garment the character does not own reads perfectly well to a human.
Three details matter more than the feature:

It fires before the output directory exists**, inside each of the seven payload builders. Nothing in this repository submits — the builders write files and a session submits them — so the irreversible step this tree owns is *writing a payload*. A refusal leaves no directory behind to be mistaken for work that happened.

name: facet v0.7.0
body: The gate closes fail-closed, a generation gets an identity, and a surface starts becoming a set of faces.**
v0.6.0 made the canon data and put a gate in front of the spend. This release closes the
three holes that were still in it — the gate was optional, a generation could not be
replayed, and a canon surface was still only a *word*.
The v0.6.0 gate read `if args.canon:`. Omit the flag and it did not run, and nothing said
so — and `texpass_loop.ps1`, the shipped driver, called `texpass_brush` without a profile.

name: v0.1.1 — E14 closes: the LoRA scene-lever priced live
body: A patch-scale state of the record, cut the same day as v0.1.0. Nothing here installs from a registry — a version in this repo marks **a state of the record**, and the record is the tree.

What this state adds.** The fourteenth experiment is closed: E14, the LoRA scene-lever bake-off, ran two arms against the byte-pinned E12 wave-3 graph — two generations, a ceiling reached exactly, zero partner credits — and the transfer premise the spec marked ASSUMED came back live on both: **a T2V-trained style LoRA binds visibly on the Fun-Camera derivative weights.** The verdicts of record, at the Director's eye: the style transform held on both arms; **the character held on `technically_color` and failed on the SmartphoneSnapshot pair.** The winner carries its caveats in the open — a served-file expert tier no gate could resolve (reported NOT VISIBLE, never faked) and a grant whose `allowNoCredit: false` puts a renderartist credits line on any published footage from that arm.

The instruments that ran it ride this state: the in-repo LoRA arm builder with the break-aware Gate LEDGER and the new **Gate PAIR_TIER** (a crossed tier-labeled pair raises; an unlabeled file is reported honestly), the byte-pinned E12 fixture so both arms rebuild from the repo alone, and a sheet composer that stopped lying twice — four regression tests riding the fix. Consult #11 joins the channel record: the GLB→2.5D-sprite side question, ruled reference-not-route with the local catalog''s limits banked.
Suite at this state: **1183 passed, 13 skipped** on the rig, under `-O` too. Translations landed before the tag, in all seven languages, as the release law orders.

Full detail: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/mcp-tool-shop-org/armature/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · the ruling: [E14-closing-ruling.md](https://github.com/mcp-tool-shop-org/armature/blob/v0.1.1/docs/experiments/E14-closing-ruling.md)

name: v0.1.0 — the first marked state of the record
body: armature's first marked state of the record: twelve experiments closed, a thirteenth dispatched, three routes, and the instruments and laws they earned. Nothing here installs from a registry — a version in this repo marks **a state of the record**, and the record is the tree.

You block the shot. The model shoots it.** armature is image-to-video with a GLB instead of an image: a canonical character mesh is staged and animated in headless Blender, and the render becomes the per-frame control sequence and reference stack a video model paints life over — so the footage carries one persistent main character whose position and pose are known every frame.

The instruments** — headless-Blender staging and render, the control-channel encoders, per-tier payload builders, the rig line, and the measurement and sheet tools every experiment is read off. **1005 tests passing on the rig** (13 skipped visibly), run twice: the second pass under `-O` proves the gates raise rather than `assert`.

The gates** — G1 legality · G2 completeness · G4 bbox · G5 convention · G6 subject motion · R round-trip · B batching · S seeds · N rig names · P rest pose · D determinism · ROUTE · PAIR · the break-aware LEDGER · BACKDROP. Each was earned by a specific silent failure and carries that story in its docstring.

The routes** — the **driven route** (rig-rendered pose sticks → the Animate tier; proven at shot level, parked for AI-animation buildout) · the **free route** (GLB-authored start frame → the camera tier at the 6.0 / uni_pc baseline; identity holds unanchored, and a handed world holds to the last frame on two seeds) · the **composed route** (authored references into a hosted identity-lock tier; under probe, dispatched with its per-route disclosure note riding the spec).

The record** — `docs/experiments/` carries E01–E13 as spec → report → ruling with amendments appended in place; `docs/license-map.md` holds a retrieved licence document for every adopted dependency, UNVERIFIED treated as NO; withdrawn approaches stay runnable in-tree, because a falsified approach that leaves the tree becomes doctrine again.

name: v0.1.0 - the extraction, with its own suite

455 checks across all ten modules, CI on Python 3.11 and 3.13, two adversarial fixture record-repos.
Stdlib only (sqlite3 + re + json) - a declared property, not an accident. No runtime dependencies.

Four known defects, reproduced and pinned in-tree as strict-xfail tests, named in the README and on the landing page: verify() doubles diagnostic counts (gating legs unaffected); the claim-arc pattern assumes E-numbered arcs; the sub-ruling locator is not derived from the declared header form; four declaration fields cannot be declared honestly empty. None affects the current consumers; all queued for 0.1.1.

README in eight languages.

name: v4.6.0 — the Forge→Engine content contract
body: Where v4.5.0 closed the authoring→Godot loop, this release closes the authoring→**runtime** loop: an exported pack boots into a played session instead of merely passing `validate`.

Forge↔Engine alignment audit** (`docs/c0-alignment/`) — a leaf-path differ walks every authored field and records which ones actually reach the runtime, generated and verified on every test run. "What survives export" is now a checked-in number rather than an assumption.

Manifest truth** — the emitted pack carries a real engine semver range, real module ids, a content hash, and compiled exit conditions. Module ids are gated on real content: a pack with no crafting stations no longer claims the crafting module.
The space vocabulary crosses** — per-entity placements with compiled spawn conditions, typed hazards, entry gates, and scene descriptors reach the engine's content pack, not just the schema.
The stage lane** — the Salt Road authored world, fixture exporters, and an unparseable-scene guard.
Engine dependency range `2.x` → `^3.8.0`.
